alt: Text A is a narrative of about 900 words from the twentieth or twenty-first century. Section A carries 25 marks on it: Question 1, a series of short answers, is worth 16 and Question 2 is worth 9. Question 1 tests R1, explicit meanings, and R2, implicit meanings and attitudes.
caption: Question 1 is 16 of Section A’s 25 marks, split between explicit and implicit meaning.

after: ## Explicit and implicit: two different jobs
alt: Above the surface line, explicit (R1) answers are stated in the text, as in asking what two things Amira noticed. Below it, implicit (R2) answers are inferred: what Amira does, what she avoids and how the narrator describes her lead to the conclusion that she is afraid of her uncle.
caption: Explicit answers are found; implicit answers are inferred and anchored in a detail.

alt: Command words rise from identify (pick out a detail) and give (state it from the text) to explain (give reasons with evidence). Five common wordings each ask for something different: own-words meaning, an explanation in context, an inference, exactly two points, or an exact short quotation.
caption: The wording of the sub-question tells you what kind of answer earns the mark.

after: ## Matching the answer to the marks
alt: One mark needs one point, a phrase or short sentence; two marks need two separate points or a point and its explanation, made visible; three marks need three points or an inference with developed support. Writing more does not add marks.
caption: Count the marks, then give that many distinct points.

alt: Three methods for own-words answers: replace key words (reluctant becomes unwilling), unpack the phrase (her voice was brittle becomes she sounded tense, as if she might break down) and change the grammar (his hesitation becomes he paused because he was unsure).
caption: Re-express the key words; leave the everyday ones alone.

alt: Four details from the Daniel extract each feed one sub-question: the late bus answers (a) for one mark; thirty heads turning is explained in own words for (b); letting go of the railing and taking hold again shows hesitation for (c); and the unsigned permission slip supports one of two reasons in (d).
caption: Each mark-earning answer is anchored in one precise detail of the text.
